correctness.rationale: For distinct 0≤a<b<1, Γ=VV* with two independent geometric columns. Hence its nonzero spectrum is exactly the positive 2×2 Cauchy-Gram spectrum, with trace T and determinant D. The reversible product parameterization p=ab∈[0,(T−2)/T) yields D=(T−2−Tp)/((1−p)^2(1+p)); q=a²+b²=(T−2+Tp²)/(T−1), and q²−4p²=((1−p²)((T−2)²−T²p²))/(T−1)²>0 recover both poles uniquely for each p. The derivative sign is controlled by Q=Tp²+(3−T)p+1 with discriminant (T−1)(T−9), proving strict uniqueness through T=9 and exactly three monotone branches above. Cubic cross-multiplication excludes a fourth preimage. The T=9 Taylor coefficient is exact. The included check.py passed 3708 numerical/exact-rational supplementary assertions, not treated as infinite proof.

value.rationale: For a known equal-unit-amplitude two-exponential moment response, inverse spectral observation consists naturally of the two positive operator eigenvalues. The theorem fully characterizes when these data identify the two decay rates, with a sharp trace-nine transition and an open region of genuine three-to-one ambiguity even though the masses are fixed. Its reversible cubic and cubic critical flattening illuminate conditioning and identifiability in compact rank-two Hankel inverse problems; it is not a routine norm evaluation or an unmotivated parameter slice.
